headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Aider edits a shared repo that OpenMetadata can access via MCP/APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared repo, while OpenMetadata can expose context through MCP/APIs/webhooks. If OpenMetadata content is copied into repo files or prompts, Aider may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is written into files Aider reads as instructions, injection becomes reachable.
IF the shared repo is used as a message bus between the agents, prompt hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Separate instruction files from data files in the repo.
Add a fixed prompt delimiter and ignore instructions from repo content.
Require human review before Aider acts on OpenMetadata-generated text.
Use a read-only export from OpenMetadata for any content fed to Aider.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad filesystem read/write and can send context to configured model providers, while OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory metadata and can expose data through APIs/MCP. If sensitive metadata is placed in the shared repo or passed through Aider prompts, it can leak to third-party inference. The profiles support the pathway, but not a direct breach.
conditions: IF sensitive governance or lineage data is stored in the shared repo, Aider may transmit it to its model provider.
IF OpenMetadata API responses are pasted into Aider prompts, those contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Redact secrets and identifiers before sharing data with Aider.
Restrict Aider to a scrubbed working tree.
Disable or review outbound model-provider calls for sensitive tasks.
Use synthetic metadata samples for cross-agent workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its shared-state model is via a shared git repo. OpenMetadata is runnable and uses MCP/APIs/events/webhooks, so both agents can mutate overlapping project artifacts or metadata flows. With no locking or coordination shown, concurrent writes can clobber each other; uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo or metadata-backed resource, conflicts are reachable.
IF OpenMetadata emits events/webhooks that trigger writes while Aider is committing, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Serialize writes with a single operator-controlled queue.
Assign disjoint paths or namespaces to each agent.
Pause one agent during the other's commit window.
Add a pre-commit diff check for overlapping edits.
requires-engineering: implement resource locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and commits, while OpenMetadata can surface lineage, governance, and trust metadata that may be consumed as authoritative context. If OpenMetadata output is fed into Aider without verification, Aider can encode errors into commits or downstream metadata updates. The pairwise pathway exists, but no direct automation loop is documented.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are used as ground truth for Aider edits, errors can cascade into git history.
IF Aider commits changes based on unverified metadata, downstream consumers may inherit the mistake.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before commits.
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against source-of-truth systems.
Limit Aider to draft-only changes until reviewed.
Tag provenance on any metadata imported from OpenMetadata.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and provider API keys, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge via APIs and MCP. If regulated or sensitive metadata is stored in the shared repo or sent through OpenMetadata integrations, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared repo, retention and access controls must be aligned.
IF OpenMetadata integrations export metadata to external services, residency or logging obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Classify data before either agent touches it.
Keep regulated records out of the shared repo.
Review retention settings on OpenMetadata integrations.
Document which provider receives Aider prompts.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
